The vi/vim is pretty easy to use if you got used to some basic commands. If you don't like it, you could try out nano or mc.

Cheatsheet

:q[uit]! without write

:e[dit]! reload/edit current file disgarding changes
:e[dit] {file} edit filename
:w[rite] write to file
:wq write to file and exit
:wq {file} write to filename
:r[ead] [name] insert file below

h/j/k/l move left/down/up/right
Home/End home/end current line
G/gg begin/end of file
:{line#} goto line number

i insert at cursor
a append at cursor
A append at end of line
o/O insert newline below/above
:d[elete] {nlines} delete nlines from current line, also copy to buffer
:y[ank] {nlines} copy n lines from current line, default 1 line
p/P paste after/before cursor
gp/P paste & go to end

v/V select char/line: then 
 d(delete & copy to buffer), y(yank/copy), c(change), ~(switch case), <(shift left), >(shift right)

/{pattern}[/] search/highlight pattern then
